title: Structs Aren't on the Stack. How C# Actually Manages Memory.
why_read: A clear technical correction of a widespread C#/.NET memory-model misconception, useful for any C# developer who wants to actually understand GC and performance.
analysis: This article challenges the oversimplified 'structs on stack, classes on heap' rule taught in most C# courses, explaining what the CLR actually does with struct and class instances in memory. The real behavior is more nuanced: structs can end up on the heap when boxed or stored inside a class, and understanding this matters for diagnosing GC pauses and mutability bugs. This is a genuinely useful, correctness-focused explainer on a topic many working C# developers get wrong, making it solid technical content despite being an introductory-level piece.
